sub.en: Look at the sentences. Which words go with positives, which with negatives and questions?

use: I haven’t seen anything like this.
tts: Here I am in Tokyo. It’s eleven p.m. and I’m standing outside a Manga Kissa. What, you might ask, is a Manga Kissa?
Well, Kissa is a Japanese word for café and Manga are Japanese comic books. And this is where I’m going to stay the night.
But don’t worry, I’ve done my research, and according to my guidebook, Manga cafés are a good choice if you’re looking for somewhere cheap to spend the night. Manga cafés are everywhere in Japan.
I haven’t seen anything like this before. Nobody’s serving food, but if I need something to eat there are loads of vending machines. Everyone leaves their shoes outside the room.

acts.title: Three people, one week, no agreement
text: We have been trying to book a holiday for eleven days. There are three of us and we want three different things, which is the whole problem.

Aigul wants somewhere hot with nothing to do. Her exact words were “I want to be bored for a week.” She has already sent us four links to remote self-catering places where the nearest shop is forty kilometres away.
Marat wants somewhere with something happening every evening. He says a week with nothing to do is not relaxing, it is boring, and that these are different words for a reason.
I want somewhere neither of them has been, because I am tired of hearing about the trip to Georgia in 2019.
Nobody has booked anything yet. The flights have gone up twice while we argued. We might end up going nowhere at all, which — and I have not said this out loud — would suit Aigul perfectly.

write.q: Describe the holiday you want and the one you don’t: 6 sentences. Use somewhere, anywhere, nothing or nobody at least three times between them, and use one -ed adjective and one -ing adjective correctly.
write.model: I want to go somewhere hot where there is almost nothing to do. I haven’t been anywhere near the sea for four years and I am starting to take it personally. I don’t want a city where everyone has a list of things you must see; that kind of week is exhausting rather than relaxing. Nobody in my family agrees with me — my brother says a beach is boring after two days. He gets bored on the way to the airport. We will probably end up somewhere in the mountains, which is nobody’s first choice and everybody’s second.

speak.q: Answer out loud: Where do you want to go on holiday? Is there anywhere you would never go? What kind of week do you find relaxing, and what do you find boring?
speak.model: I want to go somewhere hot with nothing to do. I wouldn’t go anywhere with a long list of museums. A week by the sea is relaxing for me. A city where everyone is in a hurry is exhausting — and after two days it’s boring too.
